## sheet: Sheet1
TO:	Debbie-Anne Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission						
FROM:	Center for Biological Diversity (19,935 supporters)						
RE:	Docket no. P-15423-000						
							
First Name	Last Name	City	State/Province	Zip/Postal	Subject	Comment	Date Submitted
Steven	Prince	Eugene	OR	97405	Deny the Cook Inlet underwater data center permit (docket no. P-15423-000)	I urge the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to deny the preliminary permit for the DeepGreen Cook Inlet Subsea-Compute & Infrastructure Hub (docket no. P-15423-000). The permit would authorize activities that pose a risk to endangered Cook Inlet beluga whales. In addition, the application raises important questions regarding the scope of the proposed activities and their potential effects on wildlife and habitat.   Although this application seeks a preliminary permit, the surveys and studies undertaken to evaluate the project could themselves affect belugas through vessel traffic, underwater noise, and other disturbances. Cook Inlet belugas are highly sensitive to such impacts and continue to face significant cumulative threats throughout their habitat.   For these reasons, the commission should *not* approve the permit. If FERC nevertheless proceeds, it must ensure robust measures to avoid impacts to beluga whales and their habitat and ensure full compliance with applicable environmental laws.	2026-10-16 00:00:00

Save Beluga Whales From a Data Center
November 2, 2026

We, the 19,935 undersigned, urge the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to deny the preliminary permit for the
DeepGreen Cook Inlet Subsea-Compute & Infrastructure Hub (docket no. P-15423-000). The permit would authorize
activities that pose a risk to endangered Cook Inlet beluga whales. In addition, the application raises important questions
regarding the scope of the proposed activities and their potential effects on wildlife and habitat.

Although this application seeks a preliminary permit, the surveys and studies undertaken to evaluate the project could
themselves affect belugas through vessel traffic, underwater noise, and other disturbances. Cook Inlet belugas are highly
sensitive to such impacts and continue to face significant cumulative threats throughout their habitat.

For these reasons, the commission should *not* approve the permit. If FERC nevertheless proceeds, it must ensure
robust measures to avoid impacts to beluga whales and their habitat and ensure full compliance with applicable
environmental laws.
